hints.title: Single-Pass Coordinate Validation Obstacle
hints.text: Checking each row, column, and subgrid in separate passes visits cells multiple times. How can you validate row uniqueness, column uniqueness, and subbox uniqueness simultaneously in a single pass over the board?

hints.title: Subgrid Formula and Bit Tracking
hints.text: Map row and column coordinates to a subbox index using integer division. For each non-empty digit, confirm it has not been recorded previously in the corresponding row, column, or subbox.

hints.title: Single Pass Board Validation Procedure
hints.text: Create 9 row sets, 9 column sets, and 9 box sets. Traverse row r from 0 to 8 and column c from 0 to 8. If board[r][c] is not a period, calculate box index (r // 3) * 3 + (c // 3). If the character exists in rows[r], cols[c], or boxes[box_idx], return false. Otherwise insert the character into all three sets. Return true if all filled cells are valid.

hints.title: Complete Implementation

complexity.notes: Single pass validation of 81 cells using fixed constant space.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Separate iterations for each row, column, and subgrid perform 243 cell checks instead of a streamlined 81-step single pass.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Tracking seen digits per region allows instantaneous O(1) duplicate detection without repeatedly scanning rows or columns.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Correct subbox indexing formula (r // 3) * 3 + (c // 3) and handling empty cells efficiently.
